newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil CVRD wants to prevent break-up of company.
newsitem.headline: Brazil CVRD wants to prevent break-up of company.

text.p: Brazil's soon to be privatized Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) wants to ensure that its mines-to-railway-to-port operations will not be broken up after privatization, a company spokesman said.
He said the company has drawn up a proposal that would bar the future owners of CVRD from selling company assets worth more than one percent of total assets.
CVRD believes its integrated production structure is the key to maintaining the company's efficiency.

Under CVRD's sell-off plan the government would retain two "golden shares" in the privatized company, which would give it veto powers over any attempt to spin off CVRD's iron ore, railway or port operations.
CVRD welcomes the "golden shares" but it wants their content to be defined more precisely, the spokesman said.

The company's proposal, which has been presented to the government and to the consortium which is in charge of CVRD's privatization modalities, is being studied by the National Privatization Council (CND), the spokesman said.
An initial 40-45 percent chunk of CVRD's voting shares, which will constitute a holding dubbed Valecom, is due to be sold off in February 1997.
Immediately after the block sale, 10 percent of CVRD's total capital will be offered to company staff, and a pubic offering on international and domestic markets will follow from June 1997 on.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
